QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_35

question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF, open-ended, daily NAV) receives a grievance from Ms. Priya Shah on 1 May 2026 about delay in redemption settlement. The Manager submits its ATR on SCORES on 18 May 2026. The investor requests first review on 25 May 2026, but feels the revised ATR is inadequate. Within how many calendar days of receiving the revised ATR can the investor approach SEBI for a SECOND review, and what happens meanwhile?

answer.text: Within 15 calendar days; SEBI may take cognizance and intervene; the complaint is resolved/disposed/closed only when SEBI 'disposes' or 'closes' it on SCORES.
Within 365 calendar days; the ATR stands finally resolved after the first review.
Only at AGM; SEBI has no role.
Never — Cat III investors cannot request a second review.

explanation.text: The Logic: An investor may request a SECOND review within 15 calendar days of receiving the revised ATR. SEBI may take cognizance via SCORES and intervene. The complaint is 'resolved/disposed/closed' only when SEBI itself disposes or closes it on SCORES. The Trap: The other options misstate the timeline/outcome or contradict the SEBI Facilitation Regulations. Note: Pages 282-283 of the workbook set the 15-calendar-day second-review window, the SEBI cognizance/intervention step, and the SCORES-disposed/closed completion condition.
